newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Regaining some lost territory.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Regaining some lost territory.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose from 1/8 to 3/8 of a point in early afternoon trade on Thursday, as the most recent economic data supported reports seen earier that showed inflation was not taking flight.

Gains were concentrated in the long end of the cash municipal market, but a trader noted that just as these bonds had resisted falling as steeply as Treasuries, they now were failing to match all the turn higher.

While secondary market activity picked up from slow levels seen early this week, it still was fairly moderate, and traders said dealers likely were trying to sell bonds that they had bought at losses.

"I think people just are relieved their inventory hasn't been marked down more than it has been," a trader said. Later, he added, "There are probably a fair amount of shops that have situations they have to work off."
A few bid wanted lists from both Wall Street dealers and brokers were being circulated.

When consumer spending, which accounts for two-thirds of the U.S. economy, on Wednesday was reported to have climbed 0.6 percent, just a bit less than forecast, the Treasury market responded with big gains.
The positive tone intensified on Thursday, as the market responded to a moderate 0.2 percent rise in the Consumer Price Index for July, which matched forecasts.

And a modest, 0.2 percent gain in industrial production reported by the Federal Reserve also mirrored forecasts, and was at least partly countered by a drop in capacity utilization to 83.1 percent from a downwardly revised reading of 83.3 percent in June.
"We've gotten through the landmine, I guess you could say," a trader said. "Hopefully, we can get some of the refundings that were lost."

When the Treasury market nosedived over fears that consumers might have splurged in July, a number of municipal issuers were forced to delay refundings as they no longer stood to capture enough savings.
In the secondary market, E-470 Public Highway Authority, Colorado, Revenues of 2026, which pay a five percent coupon, were offered at 5.46 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Bay Transportation Authority bonds of 2024, which also carry a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.53 percent, NET, down five basis points.
In Chicago futures markets, the September municipal bond futures jumped 25 ticks to 119-25/32. The climb was mirrored by Treasury bonds, which rose 25 ticks to 113-21/32.
The MOB spread stood at plus 192 ticks.
